title: The City and the Field — the Cry-Out Rule and the Bride-Price Marriage
penalty: City case: both parties stoned. Field case: the man alone dies; the woman is explicitly cleared, 'there is... no sin worthy of death.' Unbetrothed case: fifty shekels to the father and mandatory, permanent marriage, with the perpetual-marriage clause functioning as the woman's only stated 'remedy.'
summary: Three linked cases graded entirely by geography and evidence, not by consent: a betrothed woman assaulted in the city is presumed complicit and stoned alongside her attacker because a city-dweller could theoretically be heard; the same woman assaulted in an open field is presumed innocent, because no one could have heard her cry for help; and an unbetrothed virgin who is 'found' with a man must be married to him for life, at a fixed bride-price, with no right of divorce ever granted him.

title: Put Away Leaven; Eat Unleavened Bread (the Purge)
penalty: Being 'cut off from Israel' — the same karet exclusion as the uncircumcised.
summary: During the seven days of Unleavened Bread, all leaven must be purged from the house and only unleavened bread eaten; eating leavened bread means being 'cut off from Israel.'

title: Gather Daily, Leave None Till Morning (the Manna Rule)
penalty: The hoarded portion spoils — 'bred worms, and stank.' The punishment is built into the bread.
summary: The manna in the wilderness had to be gathered daily and eaten the same day; what was hoarded 'bred worms and stank.' A law of daily dependence and against accumulation.

title: No Other Gods
penalty: None stated here; elsewhere death (Ex 22:20, Deut 13:6-10) and covenant curses.
summary: The first commandment: exclusive allegiance to YHWH. No rival deities may be acknowledged, worshipped, or ranked alongside him.

title: No Graven Images
penalty: None stated in the verse; idolaters elsewhere face death (Deut 27:15 curses the image-maker).
summary: Prohibits manufacturing carved cult images — read literally, any likeness of anything in sky, earth, or sea.

title: No Bowing to or Serving Images; Transgenerational Punishment
penalty: Divine sanction: iniquity 'visited' on descendants to the third and fourth generation.
summary: Forbids venerating or serving images, and attaches a sanction principle: guilt runs downstream three to four generations; loyalty earns mercy to thousands.

title: The Name Not in Vain
penalty: 'The LORD will not hold him guiltless' — divine sanction; blasphemy earns death by stoning in Lev 24:16.
summary: Forbids empty, deceitful, or profane use of God's name — in its original setting, chiefly false oaths sworn by YHWH.

title: Remember the Sabbath
penalty: Death (Ex 31:14-15, Numbers 15:32-36); here, none stated.
summary: Mandates a weekly work stoppage for the whole household economy — children, servants, livestock, and resident foreigners included — grounded in God's rest after creation.

title: Honor Father and Mother
penalty: None here (reward stated instead); striking or cursing a parent is death (Ex 21:15,17); the incorrigible son is stoned (Deut 21:18-21).
summary: Positive duty of honor toward both parents, with a stated reward: long tenure in the land. The only commandment with an attached promise.

title: Thou Shalt Not Kill
penalty: Death for murder (Ex 21:12); exile to refuge for manslaughter (Num 35).
summary: Prohibits unlawful killing. The Hebrew verb (ratsach) targets murder and manslaughter of persons within the community, not all killing — war, execution, and animal slaughter proceed under other statutes.

title: No Adultery
penalty: Death for both parties (Leviticus 20:10, Deuteronomy 22:22).
summary: Prohibits adultery — in its original legal sense, intercourse with another man's wife or betrothed; a property-and-paternity offense against the husband.

title: No Stealing
penalty: Restitution: double for possession, four sheep or five oxen for slaughtered/sold animals (Ex 22:1,4); sold into servitude if unable to pay (Ex 22:3).
summary: Prohibits theft of property (and, on one ancient reading, theft of persons — kidnapping, cf. Ex 21:16).

title: No False Witness
penalty: Talionic: 'then shall ye do unto him, as he had thought to have done unto his brother' (Deut 19:19) — up to death for false capital testimony.
summary: Prohibits perjured testimony against a member of the community; the integrity clause of a legal system that runs entirely on witnesses.

title: No Coveting
penalty: None stated; unenforceable by human courts by design.
summary: Prohibits desiring what belongs to a neighbor — house, wife, servants, livestock. The Decalogue's only regulation of a mental state; also its plainest inventory of persons as property.

title: No Gods of Silver or Gold
penalty: None stated; the calf episode answers with plague and sword (Ex 32:27-28,35).
summary: Restates the image ban with specificity: no manufacturing deities from precious metals, even as companions ('with me') to YHWH's worship.

title: Altar of Earth; Sacrifice Where the Name Is Recorded
penalty: None stated.
summary: Prescribes simple earthen altars for burnt and peace offerings, valid at every place God 'records his name' — a decentralized, multi-site sacrificial system.

title: No Hewn Stone Altars
penalty: The altar is 'polluted' — ritually void.
summary: Stone altars must be of uncut fieldstone; applying a tool pollutes the altar.

title: No Steps Up to the Altar
penalty: None stated; for priests, wrongful exposure at the altar risks death (Ex 28:43).
summary: Altars may not be approached by steps, lest the officiant's genitals be exposed beneath his robe while climbing.

title: Hebrew Servant Freed in the Seventh Year
penalty: None stated for violation; Jeremiah 34:17 has God sentence release-violators to 'liberty... to the sword.'
summary: Debt servitude of a Hebrew man is capped at six years; in the seventh he goes free without payment, with the wife he brought in.

title: Master Keeps the Wife He Gave, and Her Children
penalty: None; this is an allocation rule.
summary: If the master supplied the servant's wife, she and their children remain the master's property at release; the man goes free alone.

title: The Awl and the Doorpost: Perpetual Service Election
penalty: None; a voluntary (nominally) status change, irrevocable.
summary: A servant may renounce his seventh-year release by formal declaration before the judges; his ear is bored through with an awl at the doorpost and he serves permanently.

title: Daughter Sold as Maidservant; Redemption Rights
penalty: Loss of resale rights for the deceitful master; redemption must be permitted.
summary: A father may sell his daughter as a maidservant-concubine; she is not released on the six-year schedule, but if the master who took her for himself rejects her, she must be allowed redemption and cannot be resold abroad.

title: Maidservant Betrothed to the Son: Daughter's Rights
penalty: None stated; vv.10-11 supply the exit remedy for maintenance failures.
summary: If the purchaser assigns the maidservant to his son, her status converts: she must be treated as a daughter of the house, not a servant.

title: Food, Raiment, and Marriage Duty Not Diminished
penalty: Automatic manumission without redemption payment.
summary: A man who takes an additional wife must not reduce the first's food, clothing, or conjugal rights; failure on any of the three frees her without payment.

title: Death for Striking a Man Fatally
penalty: Death.
summary: Fatal assault is a capital offense — the apodictic baseline that vv.13-14 immediately grade by intent.

title: A Place to Flee for the Unintentional Killer
penalty: Exile to refuge in lieu of death; leaving early forfeits protection (Num 35:26-28).
summary: Killing without premeditation ('God delivered him into his hand') is not capital; the killer flees to an appointed place of asylum.

title: Take the Murderer from the Altar
penalty: Death, asylum notwithstanding.
summary: Premeditated murder voids all asylum — even a killer clinging to God's own altar is dragged off and executed.

title: Death for Striking Father or Mother
penalty: Death.
summary: Striking either parent — not killing, striking — is a capital offense.

title: Death for Manstealing
penalty: Death.
summary: Kidnapping a person for sale — or being caught holding the victim — is a capital offense.

title: Death for Cursing Father or Mother
penalty: Death (Lev 20:9 adds 'his blood shall be upon him').
summary: Cursing — invoking harm on, or contemptuously repudiating — a parent is a capital offense. Speech alone suffices.

title: Assault: Lost Time and Full Healing
penalty: Compensatory damages: lost time plus complete cure. No further liability.
summary: Non-fatal fight injuries are settled civilly: the striker pays for the victim's lost work time and full medical recovery, then is quit.

title: Beating a Servant: Punished Only If Death Is Swift
penalty: Unspecified punishment ('avenged') for immediate death; nothing if death is delayed.
summary: A master who beats a slave to immediate death is punished; if the slave lingers a day or two before dying, there is no penalty — 'for he is his money.'

title: Striking a Pregnant Woman: Fine for the Lost Pregnancy
penalty: Judicially ratified fine, amount proposed by the husband.
summary: If brawling men injure a pregnant woman and she miscarries but suffers no further harm ('no mischief'), the offender pays a fine set by the husband and ratified by judges.

title: Life for Life, Eye for Eye
penalty: Mirror injury (or its monetary equivalent, per the entire subsequent legal tradition).
summary: The lex talionis: where lasting harm follows, the penalty mirrors the injury exactly — life, eye, tooth, hand, foot, burn, wound, stripe.

title: Servant Freed for a Destroyed Eye or Tooth
penalty: Mandatory manumission of the injured slave.
summary: A master who destroys a slave's eye or tooth must free the slave — manumission as the damages award, in place of talion.

title: The Goring Ox: Stone the Ox, Owner Quit
penalty: Stoning of the ox; flesh unusable; owner exempt (first offense).
summary: An ox that kills a person is stoned and its meat is taboo; the owner of a first-offense ox bears no liability. The rule applies equally when the victim is a child.

title: The Known Goring Ox: Owner Dies, Unless Ransomed
penalty: Death for the owner, commutable by assessed ransom; ox stoned regardless.
summary: If the ox was a known gorer, formally attested to the owner, and he failed to confine it, a killing makes the owner capitally liable — though uniquely, he may ransom his life for whatever sum is assessed.

title: Ox Gores a Servant: Thirty Shekels to the Master
penalty: Thirty shekels of silver to the slave's master; ox stoned. The slave's estate receives nothing.
summary: When the victim is a slave, capital exposure vanishes: the owner pays the slave's master thirty shekels; the ox is still stoned.

title: The Open Pit: Digger Pays for the Fallen Beast
penalty: Full value compensation to the animal's owner; salvage to the payer.
summary: Whoever opens or digs a pit and leaves it uncovered pays the owner of any ox or ass that falls in; the carcass belongs to the payer.

title: Ox Gores Ox: Split the Live One, Split the Dead
penalty: No-fault: equal division of live-ox proceeds and carcass. Negligence: full ox-for-ox replacement, salvage to payer.
summary: When one ox kills another: no-fault case, sell the live ox and split both proceeds and carcass; known-gorer case, the negligent owner pays full replacement and keeps the dead animal.

title: The Holy Seed Mingled — Foreign Contact Defiles
penalty: Expulsion of the foreign spouse and the children of the union ('put away all the wives, and such as are born of them').
summary: Returned exiles who intermarried with the peoples of the surrounding lands are held to have defiled 'the holy seed' by contact itself; Ezra leads a covenant to 'put away' the foreign wives and their children as the remedy.

title: Circumcision on the Eighth Day (the Covenant Sign)
penalty: Being 'cut off from his people' — covenant exclusion, the loss of belonging itself.
summary: Every male is circumcised on the eighth day as the physical token of the covenant; the uncircumcised is 'cut off' — excluded from the covenant people.

title: The Seed Not Spilled (Onan) — the Biological Sanctity Doctrine
penalty: Death, by God directly.
summary: Onan, refusing to father a child for his dead brother, 'spilled his seed on the ground' and God killed him — the narrative from which a whole doctrine of the sanctity and proper destination of 'seed' is derived.

title: Uncleanness Spreads by Touch; Holiness Does Not
penalty: Not punitive in itself; it is the stated mechanism by which contact renders a person, offering, or object unclean, which then triggers whatever penalty attaches to the resulting impurity.
summary: A priestly ruling, given as a formal legal question-and-answer: consecrated holiness does not transmit by mere contact, but corpse-uncleanness does. Impurity is contagious; sanctity is not.

title: The Bread of the Presence (Showbread) — for the Priests Only
penalty: None stated; the restriction is by holiness ('most holy'), and lay consumption would profane it.
summary: Twelve cakes of fine flour are set weekly on the pure table before God; the old bread belongs to the priests alone, to be eaten in the holy place — sacred food no layman may touch.

title: The Ordeal of Jealousy (the Bitter Water)
penalty: For the 'guilty': the belly to swell and the thigh to rot — reproductive destruction, and to 'be a curse among her people.' For the husband: 'the man shall be guiltless' regardless of outcome.
summary: A husband who suspects his wife of adultery but has no witnesses brings her to the priest, who makes her drink 'bitter water'; guilt manifests as her 'belly swelling and thigh rotting' (traditionally read as a state-induced miscarriage or reproductive ruin), innocence as fertility.

title: Women Who Change the Natural Use (the Extension to Female Conduct)
penalty: None stated directly in the text; it is descriptive ('God gave them up'), not a civil statute prescribing a human penalty — unlike Leviticus 20:13's explicit capital sentence for the male case.
summary: Paul's catalogue of Gentile idolatry's consequences names both female and male same-sex conduct as evidence of a society 'given up' by God; it is the only passage in either testament that names female homosexuality by description rather than silence.
